what_its_for: Crotamiton is a medicated cream or lotion used to treat scabies, a skin condition caused by tiny mites that burrow under your skin and cause intense itching. It can also be used to relieve itching from other skin conditions.
how_to_take: Crotamiton is applied directly to your skin. Before your first application, take a warm bath or shower and dry your skin thoroughly. Apply the cream or lotion in a thin layer from your chin down to your toes, including all skin folds, between your fingers and toes, under your nails, and around your belly button. Do not apply it to your face, scalp, or inside your mouth, eyes, or vagina. A second application is usually applied 24 hours later. After 48 hours from the second application, take another bath or shower to wash off the medicine completely. Put on clean clothes and change your bed linens after treatment.
dosing: For scabies: Apply to the entire body from the chin down, once a day for two days in a row (two total applications, 24 hours apart). For itching: Apply a thin layer to the itchy area and gently massage it in. You may repeat this as needed. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as dosing may vary.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply your second dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it has been more than 24 hours since your first dose, call your doctor for guidance. Do not apply two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store crotamiton at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat and direct sunlight. Keep the cap tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not store it in the bathroom where it can get damp.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting crotamiton in your eyes, mouth, nose, or genitals. If it accidentally gets into your eyes, rinse them right away with plenty of water. Avoid applying it to open wounds, broken skin, or areas with severe rashes. Do not use more than directed, as applying too much can increase the risk of side effects. Avoid sharing towels, clothing, or bedding with others during treatment to prevent spreading scabies.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if: your skin becomes severely red, swollen, blistered, or more irritated after using the medicine; you develop a rash or signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat; the itching or scabies does not improve or gets worse after completing your full course of treatment; you accidentally swallow any of the medicine; or if other household members develop itching or similar symptoms, as they may also need treatment.
when_it_works: The itching from scabies may continue for a few weeks even after successful treatment, because your skin is still reacting to the dead mites. This is normal and does not mean the treatment failed. Most people see improvement within 1 to 2 weeks after completing treatment. If itching continues beyond 4 weeks or new burrow marks appear, contact your doctor, as a second treatment may be needed.
special_populations: Children: Crotamiton should be used with caution in infants and young children. Always follow your doctor's instructions carefully. The face and scalp may need to be included in treatment for very young children, but only if your doctor says so. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using crotamiton if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Use it only if clearly needed and directed by your healthcare provider. Elderly: Older adults may have more sensitive skin and should use this medicine carefully to avoid irritation. People with skin conditions: If you have eczema, psoriasis, or other skin conditions, check with your doctor before using crotamiton.
